h: Swanbourne Lake, Amberley and the South Downs
p: Seasons change the cast list here. Spring brings ducklings and the chatter of reed and sedge warblers in the reedbeds, summer is lush and green, and winter pulls in wild ducks to the lakes. Spotting a kingfisher's electric-blue flash along the water is the holy grail for many visitors, so keep your eyes on the edges.
Get the kids to keep a tally of everything they spot; it turns a gentle walk into a bit of a competition.

Right next door, Swanbourne Lake sits at the foot of the castle grounds and is a gorgeous spot for a walk, with wildfowl, a lakeside path and rowing boats in the warmer months. It's a lovely, easy add-on to the wetland centre, and the views back towards the castle are beautiful.

A few miles up the river, Amberley Museum is a fascinating open-air museum set in an old chalk quarry, with vintage buses, a narrow-gauge railway and traditional crafts. The South Downs National Park surrounds the area, offering fantastic walks with big views, and the South Downs Way passes nearby for keen walkers.

Time your visit right and the town has a few extra treats. Each year around the feast of Corpus Christi, the nave of Arundel Cathedral is covered with a spectacular carpet of flowers laid out in intricate patterns, a stunning sight that draws visitors from far and wide. In summer, Arundel Lido, a community-run open-air pool beside the river, is a lovely spot to cool off.
One word of caution by the water: the Arun is a fast-flowing tidal river, so keep little ones well back from the banks on riverside walks.
